levels.title: the spark
levels.blurb: googled "how do people make video games" and found python. stayed up way too late writing terrible code and never looked back.

levels.title: under the hood
levels.blurb: tore apart computers, built networks in packet tracer, learned how systems actually work. realized i cared more about what could break than how to set it up.

levels.title: going all in
levels.blurb: transferred to FIU and bet everything on cybersecurity. got Security+, built a home lab, and made hackthebox a nightly habit.

levels.title: the lab
levels.blurb: first real tech job — running a hardware lab, tutoring students, explaining things until they clicked. the kind of work that quietly makes you sharper at everything.

levels.title: cloud unlocked
levels.blurb: took a free AWS course on a whim and went deep fast. cloud security made instant sense — certified as solutions architect and started building.

levels.title: trial by fire
levels.blurb: captained a 5-person CCDC team with one week of prep against squads who trained for months. held operations under constant red team pressure and placed 16th out of 49.

levels.title: the admiral
levels.blurb: first-authored a research paper, got accepted to cyber recon 2026, and shook hands with a U.S. Cyber Command Admiral — all as a college student. curiosity compounds.

levels.title: next quest
levels.blurb: cloud, security, AI — it all connects now. the kid who googled how games work is still pulling threads, just bigger ones.
